findings.title: getCredentials dereferences myUser without a null check
findings.body: `getMyUser(user)` returns null when the user is not in the map, for example after `removeUser` or for a user imported from elsewhere. `myUser.recoveryCodes` is then dereferenced directly. Other methods such as `isConfiguredFor` and `isValid` guard against null. Because `getCredentials` is now on the path of every `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` call, this can throw an NPE during login or cleanup.

findings.title: Recovery credential returned from getCredentials loses its id and always looks unused
findings.body: `updateCredential` stores a CredentialModel with a generated id. `getCredentials` rebuilds a fresh `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)` and does not copy that id, so the returned model has a null id. It also regenerates the code state on every call, so no code is ever marked used and `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode` always returns code #0. `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` calls `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` and checks `allCodesUsed()` on the credential from `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`. For a federated credential that id is null and the used-code tracking never advances. This is only exercised with code 0, so the test hides it.

findings.title: Federated recovery credentials are never consumed or removed after use
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can now return a federated credential. The post-validation logic still assumes a local credential. It calls `removeStoredCredentialById`, which only affects local storage, and relies on `allCodesUsed()`. Nothing in the user-storage path marks a used code. A recovery code accepted by the storage (`isValid`) therefore stays valid forever, and the 'next code to enter' number never advances. This defeats the one-time-use property of recovery codes for user-storage users, and no SPI contract exists to report consumption. The behaviour should at least be handled or documented.

findings.title: Raw recovery codes are handed to user storage and old local credentials are not cleaned up
findings.body: On the local path only hashes of the codes are persisted. This helper serializes the plaintext codes as JSON and passes them to `updateCredential`, so any user storage provider receives and can persist the raw codes. That is acceptable for OTP secrets but is worth documenting for recovery codes. In addition, when the storage accepts the credential, any previously created local recovery-codes credential is not removed. `getCredential` then silently prefers the federated one, leaving a stale local credential.

findings.title: Recovery key test is thin and has sloppy details
findings.body: The test only covers the first-code happy path (code index 0) and never checks that a wrong code fails. It does not cover the local-storage fallback or credential removal, which the new `getCredential` fallback and the form authenticator change affect. The authenticator config alias contains a typo (`delayed-suthenticator-config`). A 'delayed-authenticator' with delay 0 is added without need. `org.wildfly.common.Assert.assertTrue` is used as a test assertion.
